source.title: An Adversarial Perspective on Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
source.authors: Jakub Lucki; Boyi Wei; Yangsibo Huang; Peter Henderson; Florian Tramèr; Javier Rando

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses difference-in-means directions and activation-space removal as a knowledge-recovery method against unlearning. Its reported outcomes concern WMDP hazardous-knowledge accuracy, not refusal behavior toward a user, so it does not test the claim versions. The cited 54.2% result for ablating a single refusal direction is from other work and is not recorded as a result of this study.
record.gate_note: The study computes and removes per-layer directions to recover hazardous-knowledge benchmark performance, and uses a direction-related perturbation strategy against RMU. Those outcomes are about recovery of unlearned knowledge, not rates of refusal or compliance on user requests. The paper also cites an external single-refusal-direction ablation result of 54.2%; that cited result is excluded. Values used to select layers or thresholds are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study borrows difference-in-means directional ablation (Section 4.2, citing Arditi et al.) as a knowledge-recovery attack on unlearned and DPO-trained Zephyr-7B-β models. Every outcome is WMDP or MMLU multiple-choice accuracy, scored by the highest-probability option. That score is built to bypass refusals, so it says nothing about refusal or compliance rates toward users. The directions are computed per layer on forget-set prompts, contrasting the original or benign representations with the unlearned ones. They are not the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, and no rate of refusal is reported after ablating or adding them. The only refusal-direction result in the text, 54.2% for a single refusal direction on RMU, is cited from Arditi and Chughtai (2024) and is not this study's own result. The study therefore relies on the technique as a tool and tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that current unlearning methods (RMU, NPO) obscure rather than erase hazardous knowledge. Direction ablation, finetuning on unrelated data, pruning and adaptive GCG recover most of it, so unlearning offers little advantage over safety training, and black-box evaluations are insufficient.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means directions and activation-space removal, but computes directions for unlearning-related representations, allows separate directions by transformer block, and measures recovery of WMDP knowledge rather than refusal. The paper cites the original refusal-direction result but does not reproduce it.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction source and domain affect recovery results; all-layer versus selected-layer ablation differs, and the first-principal-component result for RMU changes with chat-template use (53.7% with it, 34.1% without it).

fits_no_version.finding: Per-layer difference-in-means ablation recovers WMDP-Bio knowledge from unlearned and refusal-DPO models. RMU goes from 29.9 to 64.7, NPO from 29.5 to 45.1, DPO from 27.9 to 50.7. Results depend on the direction source, layers, domain and chat template. NPO-Cyber all-layer ablation collapses MMLU to chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning and safety-trained suppression of hazardous knowledge is mediated by removable activation directions, which difference-in-means ablation can undo, with results varying by method.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt perturbations guided by cosine similarity with the layer-7 direction bring RMU to within 2.2 p.p. of the base model on WMDP-Bio. The same perturbed prompts transfer to Mixtral-8x7B RMU, raising accuracy by up to 29%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direction-informed input perturbations defeat keyword-triggered representation-noise unlearning.

record.problems: The direction-removal outcomes are measured with WMDP knowledge accuracy rather than refusal rates. Some figure values are not reported numerically in the text. In the WMDP-Cyber NPO all-layer ablation condition, the authors report catastrophic forgetting; the corresponding direction does not yield a clean knowledge-recovery comparison. Table 8's caption says WMDP-Bio although the surrounding section identifies the results as WMDP-Cyber.
record.rows_left_out: No direction-related results were omitted. Other unlearning attacks and training interventions not based on the direction method were excluded because they do not bear on the versions of the refusal-direction claim.

untested.parts: Ablation of a harmful-minus-harmless direction measured against refusal rate. Adding a direction to induce refusal. Capability preservation judged against refusal removal.
Weight-edit abliteration of released models measured on refusal.

Whether jailbreaks act by suppressing the refusal direction. The enhanced GCG and informed perturbations target WMDP accuracy, not the refusal direction's role in refusal. Training against ablation is not tested.
Multi-direction or cone structure of refusal. The per-layer directions serve knowledge recovery, not refusal.
Separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer of a refusal direction across languages, variants or base and instruct models. The Mixtral transfer concerns prompt perturbations and WMDP accuracy.
How refusal training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.

missing.what: Chat-template orthogonalization results. WMDP-Bio: RMU 63.0, NPO 47.3, DPO 51.7. WMDP-Cyber: RMU 41.9, NPO 34.1, DPO 37.9. These bear on no version but are part of the direction-ablation results the record says it covered fully.

record.verdict_notes: The cited 54.2% single-refusal-direction ablation on RMU (Arditi and Chughtai, 2024) is external and correctly excluded. The DPO baseline is trained to output refusal strings, but outcomes are scored by option probability, which bypasses refusal, so no refusal rate is measured. Table 8's caption mislabels Cyber results as WMDP-Bio. The record's states on version-less rows should all be cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not measure whether removing the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction changes refusal or harmless-request behavior, nor whether adding it induces refusal or preserves general abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested as removal of the refusal direction.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the original refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Per-layer directions and principal components are studied for unlearning-related knowledge recovery, not as alternatives or additions to the refusal mechanism.
No separation between harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
The study does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct stages.
The study compares unlearning and safety-training methods for knowledge recovery, but does not test how refusal-training design determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
No reasoning models are tested for the refusal-direction claim.

relation.reason: It uses the DIM ablation method as a tool, and its claim 'unlearning is also mediated by specific directions' concerns unlearning, not refusal.

tranche.reason: The study borrows per-layer difference-in-means ablation (Sec. 4.2, citing Arditi et al.) as a knowledge-recovery attack. It reports only WMDP/MMLU multiple-choice accuracy, scored by the highest-probability option, and never measures refusal rates. The direction contrasts original-model and unlearned-model activations on forget prompts, not harmful vs. harmless instructions.

source_check.notes: The Table 1 values come from runs without the chat template. The same ablation gives different numbers elsewhere in the paper. Table 7 'ground_truth' gives RMU 64.9, NPO 45.7 and DPO 56.1. Chat-template Table 11 gives 63.0, 47.3 and 51.7. The 54.2% for single-direction ablation on RMU is cited from Arditi & Chughtai 2024 (LessWrong), not measured here. 'As an AI...' lines are dataset refusal strings, not instructions.
